items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: his name was Leonard Fields, and he was a fantastic player. Gee, he got over the instrument like crazy and, gee, I don’t know that he ever recorded.

ctx.x: Some quote, unquote “jazz musicians” have mentioned that Rudy Wiedoft inspired them, not what he was playing so much as just what could be done on the instrument. Do you remember him?

Oh, definitely. He let you know what could be done on the instrument, and he let you know that he could do it, you know. It was purely technique, which was a dazzling technique for the time. Gee, I mean, there was also a player around at that time that I think came from Lexington, Kentucky, another one that nobody around today would probably remember or would have heard of, and his name was Leonard Fields, and he was a fantastic player. Gee, he got over the instrument like crazy and, gee, I don’t know that he…
You mentioned that many of the white players would come in and sit in, and you were not afforded that same reciprocal opportunity. Did you hear Jimmy Dorsey at all?

ctx.x: And I don't know how to answer that ... there was a player around dude on at the time that I must mention, but I don't know that I've heard his name mentioned recently; oh, in many years, and a lot of people would probably not have considered him a jazz saxophonist, and his name was Leonard Fields; I think he was from Lexington, or maybe Louisville, Kentucky - and if things had been a little different for the
black musician at that time, he would have been the black Wiedoeft Rudy Weedoff, you know.
